Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun, has pledged to explore the revival of the moribund Iwopin Paper Mill, construct a hospital in Ilusin and take over the completion of the new Navy School under construction in Abigi, Ogun Waterside Local Government Area. Abiodun gave the assurances during a meeting with canvassers, the local government party chairman and executive members, ward party executives and other stakeholders at the Ilusin Community Town Hall, according to a statement issued on Thursday. The governor said his administration was determined to develop Ogun Waterside and ensure that the area benefited from investment opportunities and infrastructure projects in the state. On the Iwopin Paper Mill, Abiodun acknowledged that the facility belonged to the Federal Government but said his administration would explore discussions with the Federal Government on its sale and possible revival. He said, “This facility actually belongs to the Federal Government, but our administration will explore avenues of engaging the Federal Government on revisiting its sale, with a view to restoring the industrial facility to operation. “The revival of the paper mill presents an important opportunity to stimulate industrial activities, create employment and strengthen the local economy in the local government.” The governor also assured residents of Ilusin that his administration would “build a hospital in the community to improve access to quality healthcare”. He further promised to take over and complete the new Navy School project under construction in Abigi, the headquarters of the local government area. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. He said the government had rehabilitated more than 1,600 schools and provided them with furniture to improve teaching and learning. According to him, the administration’s investments and reforms in the education sector had produced positive results, with teachers and students recording performances and winning awards at local and international competitions. He said the projects could create jobs, stimulate businesses and attract industries to the area. The governor also said his administration had facilitated the construction of more than 7,000 housing units across low-, medium- and high-income categories, while over 1,700 kilometres of roads had been constructed or rehabilitated across the state. He listed some Federal Government infrastructure projects in Ogun State as the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, the Sagamu-Ijebu-Ode-Ogbere section of the Lagos-Benin Expressway and the Ibadan-Ijebu-Ode Road. He also mentioned the approval of dry ports in Kajola and Ijebu-Ode, as well as partnerships in the industrial sector. Abiodun urged party members at the grassroots to inform residents about the achievements of the Federal, state and local governments, describing them as the party’s closest representatives to the people. He said grassroots mobilisation and communication were important to securing public support for the party and its candidates. Earlier, the Ogun State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Yemi Sanusi, urged residents to support the party’s candidates and vote for President Bola Tinubu. He said the proposed Deep Sea Port demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to the development of the area. A former Deputy Governor of Ogun State, Segun Adesegun, also described Ogun Waterside as an emerging investment destination, citing the investments planned for the area. He urged residents to familiarise themselves with the APC logo and vote for the party in the forthcoming elections. Taiwo Bankole
